subject: MAP: Lock-and-load onramp for POC environment (API keys, org setup, IP allowlist, peering)
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Johnson <emily.johnson@healright.com>, Raj Patel <raj.patel@healright.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 6 Sep 2026 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: MAP: Lock-and-load onramp for POC environment (API keys, org setup, IP allowlist, peering)

Hi Emily / Raj —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Per our call, attached is a concise mutual action plan (MAP-lockload-v1) with the minimal ops steps we need to stand up a production-like POC environment so your security and infra teams can run acceptance tests. High level ask: can HealRight commit to the items in column B by end-of-week so we can hit the target 2-week activation?

Key map items (short):
- Redwood: provide onboarding checklist, org invite, and initial API keys (scoped).
- HealRight: create POC org admin account, provide IP allowlist CIDRs, and approve VPC peering request.
- Network preflight: exchange firewall headers (see attached healright-network-headers.txt).

Immediate asks for your engineering/security teams:
1) Confirm 2 contact SROs (network + security) and their preferred contact window for a peering test.
2) Provide a list of CIDR ranges we should add to our allowlist (we will also open egress rules on our side).
3) Approve org-level invite for redwood-poc@redwood.ai (we'll send invite once you confirm admin).

Tentative timeline:
- Day 0 (this week): mutual sign-off on MAP sheet, exchange headers.
- Day 1–3: API key issuance + org invite and user provisioning.
- Day 4–7: IP allowlist and peering test.
- Day 8–14: Smoke tests, eval runs, and acceptance sign-off.

Attachments: MAP-lockload-v1.xlsx (action grid), healright-network-headers.txt, redwood-poc-onboard-checklist.pdf

If you prefer, Marcus can run the peering dry-run with your network lead — I’ve cc’d him.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference
(t) 415-555-0189

From: Emily Johnson <emily.johnson@healright.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Raj Patel <raj.patel@healright.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP: Lock-and-load onramp for POC environment (API keys, org setup, IP allowlist, peering)

Tessa — thanks for the clear plan and the attachments. Quick answers from our side:
- I'll be the security lead; Raj is infra lead. We are available for the peering test Tue–Thu morning PT.
- CIDRs: 10.48.32.0/20, 10.200.0.0/16 (internal); we can provide public egress ranges next day.
- Org admin: we need the invite sent to poc-admin@healright.com (not the redwood email you listed).

Two questions:
1) Can the API key be scoped to read-only for the first week while we run evals?
2) Do you support cross-account peering with AWS Transit Gateway (we use TGW in prod)?

We'll review the MAP spreadsheet and send a signed acknowledgement by EOD tomorrow. Attaching our network header template for your engineers.

Thanks — Emily
Emily Johnson
Director, Security & Compliance
HealRight Health

Attachment: healright-network-headers-template.txt

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Johnson <emily.johnson@healright.com>, Raj Patel <raj.patel@healright.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 8 Sep 2026 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP: Lock-and-load onramp for POC environment (API keys, org setup, IP allowlist, peering)

Emily — great, thanks. Short responses:
- API key scoping: yes, we can issue a time-limited read-only key for the first 7 days; we will mark it in our MAP sheet and rotate to full-scoped once acceptance is signaled.
- TGW peering: Redwood supports TGW-based connectivity; we have a documented TGW checklist. If you can share the TGW attachment details (account IDs and route table IDs), we can pre-populate our peering request.

Action items I’ll take now:
- I will prepare the org invite for poc-admin@healright.com and queue it for your approval.
- Drafting a minimal peering request and a stub policy for TGW that we can send to your infra team.

Small ask for HealRight infra: please confirm the AWS account IDs that will accept the peering and the preferred CIDR that Redwood should advertise back to you.

I’ll follow up with the TGW checklist and an updated MAP with the key scoping column filled.

Cheers — Marcus
Marcus Lin
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

From: Raj Patel <raj.patel@healright.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Emily Johnson <emily.johnson@healright.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 9 Sep 2026 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP: Lock-and-load onramp for POC environment (API keys, org setup, IP allowlist, peering)

Marcus / Tessa —

We reviewed the MAP and the TGW notes Marcus promised look good. Confirming:
- AWS account to accept peering: 312045678901
- Route table IDs: rtb-0a1b2c3d4e5f6a7b8 (prod-peering-stub)
- Redwood can advertise 10.81.0.0/16 back to us for the POC.
- Poc-admin@healright.com has been created and is ready for the invite.

We can run the peering acceptance test on Friday 11:00 PT; please send the peering request by EOD tomorrow and the read-only API key by tomorrow AM so we can start smoke imports.

Thanks, Raj
Raj Patel
Sr. Infra Engineer
HealRight Health
